RStudio

Setting breakpoints inside oopr classes is the same process as setting them for normal functions - use the gutter or SHIFT+F9.

RStudio calls its R functions inside tools:rstudio from the global environment. By assigning functions of the same name, these calls can be intercepted.

This feature is disabled by default as it is potentially destructive for an R session. Environmental variable R_OOPR_BREAKPOINTS=true can be used to enable this functionality when oopr namespace is loaded.

Breakpoints cannot be set on single line functions with a specifier,

get:x <- \( ) { return("x"); }

as RStudio thinks the line is at the top-level.

Tested with RStudio version 2026.1.1.403, there are no guarantees for earlier or later versions.

OoprBreakpointsRStudio

Description

The controller for RStudio breakpoints.

Details

RStudio's process of setting a breakpoint is:

  1. Check the function is in sync.

  2. Get the steps of the functions body to arrive at a line.

  3. Get the environment that the function is assigned to.

  4. Set the breakpoints into the function. Only steps 3 & 4 apply when unsetting a breakpoint, or reloading a file.

RStudio maintains its own record of breakpoints and is recorded by file and function name. However, multiple classes in a file could share a function name.

TODO: newer versions of RStudio use .rs.setBreakpoint.

getFunctionSteps

Description

Gets the "steps" required for a line.

Usage

getFunctionSteps(name, file, pkg, lines)

Arguments

lineslist()
A list of integer(1L) of the line numbers to be added.

Details

The trick here is to prefix the steps with "oopr:" as RStudio does not validate the steps field. The function setting the breakpoints will know which breakpoints are for oopr classes.

Returns

A list of list(name = character(1L), line = integer(1L), at = character(1L)), where at is in the form "oopr:line" if relating to an oopr class.
